resources.string: Center the map on my area
Map thumbnail of the place\'s verified location
Find a place, then tap its star to watch it. Kyron alerts you when a watched place gets a new inspection — set up area alerts in the Alerts tab below.
No places match. Try a different search or county.

No favorites yet.
Tap the star on any place and Kyron will watch it for you — when it gets a new inspection, you\'ll get an alert here.
Scores are public health-department records, shown as published. Alabama requires reinspection within 60 days for scores below 85.
Kyron covers states one region pack at a time, from each health department\'s own published data. A state listed as “Not covered yet” has no pack — Kyron won\'t pretend otherwise.
No alerts yet. When a place you watch gets a new inspection — or a score drops below your threshold in a county you watch — it lands here and as a notification. Set up your rules below.

Alert me when a place I watch gets a new score or inspection result — favorites always alert, on any new result. Tap the star on any restaurant to watch it. (The score threshold in the area rule below applies to area alerts.)
Alert me about bad scores in my areas
County score checks run against Alabama\'s state and county health departments. Watched places in other states alert on their new results through your favorites.
Kyron also checks for new inspections automatically about every 12 hours in the background.

No sign-up needed — Kyron works fully without an account. Your profile, favorites and alert rules stay on this device only; nothing is uploaded. They ride along in your phone\'s own Android backup when that\'s enabled, and you can export them yourself below.

America has no single restaurant-inspection database — every state and county publishes its own. Kyron is built with one adapter per source, so new states plug into this list without changing the app.

Your favorites, alert rules and inbox live only on this device (and in your phone\'s own Android backup when that\'s on). Export a backup file any time — it contains only your Kyron data, and importing it on another phone restores everything.
0–100 scores — higher is better. Every entry shows its official inspection date and the agency that published it.
Demerit points — LOWER is better (0 = a perfect inspection). Every entry shows its official inspection date and the agency that published it.
Letter grades (A/B/C) from the official grading scale. Every entry shows its inspection date and the agency that published it.
Pass / pass-with-conditions / fail outcomes. Every entry shows its inspection date and the agency that published it.
This source publishes native inspection outcomes rather than a numeric score — read the result text on each entry. Every entry shows its inspection date and the agency that published it.
This source publishes violation records without an overall result. Every entry shows its inspection date and the agency that published it.
Inspection results as published by the source agency. Every entry shows its inspection date and where the data came from.
